paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the trend of Pass@1 rate (%) on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases, comparing two large vision-language models: GPT-4o (blue line with circular markers) and Claude-3.5-Sonnet (light purple line with cross markers). The x-axis, labeled “Num. of Reasoning Steps,” spans a linear scale from 5 to 40, with major tick marks at 5, 10, 20, and 40. The y-axis, labeled “Pass@1 Rate (%)”, ranges from 0 to 100 in linear increments of 20. For GPT-4o, the Pass@1 rate starts at 6.5% at 5 steps, rises to 32.3% at 10 steps, reaches 77.4% at 20 steps, and plateaus at 83.9% at 40 steps. For Claude-3.5-Sonnet, the rate begins at 19.4% at 5 steps, increases to 38.7% at 10 steps, jumps to 87.1% at 20 steps, and slightly rises to 89.2% at 40 steps. Both models show substantial performance gains with more reasoning steps, with Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforming GPT-4o across all step counts and exhibiting a sharper initial rise followed by a slower, more gradual increase beyond 20 steps.
